360	Another thing Rabbeinu Bachyei mentions is a trait we have already discussed elsewhere; he calls it the trait of
361	hishtavut, equanimity.
362	This is a very important trait, and he mentions it in several places.
363	Hishtavut comes from the idea of evenness of soul.
364	Not in the sense of indifference, but in the sense of what we call keeping a cool head.
365	A person who loves HaShem is not shaken by anything around him.
366	Even when a disaster happens, even when there is a situation that seems
367	unclear and out of control.
368	Someone who works on hishtavut, someone who loves HaShem, is always connected to something above
369	this world, and always, always, always he is in that position of calm.
370	Another thing he says: you see it in a person's speech, all right?
371	The Name of HaShem is always on his lips, he does not curse, he says "be'ezrat HaShem." Note that Rabbeinu Bachyei says
372	here that hearts follow speech, follow actions, unlike the view that what matters, how a person
373	speaks, how a person behaves, is only what is in the heart, all right.
374	Rabbeinu Bachyei was less impressed by these "inner" people, you know, there were those
375	who like to say, "I am inward, I am..."
376	I remember a case once of a student who went around in very immodest
377	and provocative clothes and so on.
378	So I told him once, tell me how you dress, we are in a beit midrash here, respect the place and so on.
379	So he says to me, why are you looking at the externals?
380	He says, look at my inside.
381	I am a supreme tzaddik.
382	So I said to him, I want to ask you a question. I said, the shirt you are wearing, the shirt
383	is like, sorry, it was a tunic, the guy came to me in a tunic, like some,
384	I don't know, Mexican.
385	I said to him, this tunic is not something you buy cheaply in Israel.
386	It is something you have to get specially, and it also doesn't suit the climate here and so on.
387	It is much simpler to take a regular shirt.
388	That is, if you go around in this tunic, it means you want to express something
389	by what you wear.
390	Do you understand?
391	So you are what's called being without and feeling with.
392	You want to be with and feel without, I don't know how to put it.
393	It is as if, on one hand you invest in your outward appearance, in your way of speaking and so on, and on the other
394	when people tell you, how you speak, how you dress, don't pay attention to that, look inside.
395	With girls, too, it is often an issue of modesty.
396	What difference does it make how I'm dressed, look at me inside.
397	Very, very simple.
398	It is true that not everything that appears on the outside reflects what is inside.
399	But that does not mean that what appears on the outside never reflects what is inside.
400	You know, we are not teenagers here.
401	It is true that sometimes there is a person who is holy and pure, and for one reason
402	or another he dresses a certain way and speaks differently.
403	And even then, it is a question why it should be so.
404	Sometimes there is no choice, I don't know, he has no money, or
405	I don't know, he said some sentence here that he didn't really mean.
406	But if you see someone who, as they say, invested in a certain style of dress, a certain way of speaking,
407	and in...
408	and he chronically repeats the same sentences and words and...
409	then yes, as they say, if it walks like a duck, sounds like a duck, looks like a duck, it's a duck, what do you
410	want?
411	And this is what Rabbeinu Bachyei says: you want to know how a person reaches love of HaShem.
412	So he says, it is measured in this matter, how you speak and how you dress, and he
413	adds another thing, another measure of love of HaShem: a person who loves HaShem usually also brings merit to the many, that
414	is, he is also someone who tries to connect others to the service of HaShem.
415	Here too: what does it matter, I am only inward and so on.
416	Fine, true, but when you see someone who also tries to spread it further in reality, this
417	usually shows that there is someone here who is strong
418	in the matter.
419	Another thing he says, one of the signs of love for HaShem, is that a person responds correctly
420	to deeds, that is, he is happy in fulfilling mitzvot and pained when he sins.
421	All right?
422	Why am I happy precisely when I sin? That actually shows
423	that I am really a great tzaddik.
424	Come on, come on, as they say.
425	Sir, we see you are sluggish with mitzvot, you are so lethargic, and when you go to commit a transgression, you are completely
426	elated.
427	So apparently your heart is there, what can you do?
428	This is the story I once heard about someone
429	who left religious observance.
430	They asked him, why did you leave?
431	He says, listen, my father, as he told it, was a kollel student, like,
432	a married man in kollel.
433	He says, my father sat and learned Torah, and I don't know, he was dragging his feet, that's how it seemed.
434	He would arrive every morning late, all right, and return in the middle of the day.
435	He says, that is how the young man tells it, he says, only once did I see my father happy.
436	When we had to renovate the house.
437	There was once a moment, a house renovation, when there was the money and so on, so
438	he says, the first time I saw him at the store, early in the morning, comparing the marble and the prices, and he was full of
439	vitality.
440	So he said, then I understood: what makes a person happy?
441	Learning Torah does not make a person happy, and renovating a house does make a person happy.
442	So I chose that.
443	So that is what he sees, well, what do you see?
444	If you see someone who, again, when he comes to holiness, responds
445	in a very limp way.
446	And when he comes to the things of this world, he is completely blooming.
447	Then apparently his heart is in that place.
448	Fine, fine, you say, what shall I do?
449	I will work on myself, and I will try to be happy where I should be, and sad where I should not be happy.
450	Good, so that is the question now, how do you change that?
451	But Rabbeinu Bachyei says that we have measures, whether a person loves HaShem or not.
452	And another thing he says: that a person, for example, practices seclusion.
453	He praises this very much, that a person finds time with himself, for cheshbon nefesh
454	and for prayer like this, without anyone seeing him; this too is a measure of love of
455	HaShem.
456	And he also says another thing, that a person is happy and connected to other God-fearing people,
457	that he is within a society, within a community.
458	This is also a point which today, what's the importance of community?
459	I am alone and I basically am...
460	Again, anything is possible, we say, the Holy One, blessed be He, examines the kidneys and heart, but by and large, the fact
461	that a person chose to live in a certain community usually shows that he feels comfortable there.
462	Again, sometimes he comes to change it from within, all right, let's not get into that now, there is the emissary who comes, speaks
463	now not a stage, right?
464	Why did you choose to live in this neighborhood?
465	Why did you choose to live here in this settlement?
466	Why did you choose to live in this place?
467	You're not here setting up a tefillin stand.
468	You just live here and give the impression that you actually enjoy all the atmosphere around here and so on, even though there is an
469	atmosphere here of Shabbat desecration and lack of fear of Heaven and so on and so on.
470	Well, so, a question, a question.
471	Take, a person who is willing to pay economic and climate prices, right?
472	You go to live in places with a not-great climate.
473	Or not-great scenery.
474	Why?
475	Because you want you and your children to grow up in a Torah society and so on.
476	So it shows, right, love of HaShem.
477	Look, on everything Rabbeinu Bachyei shows one could go into endless nuances and subtleties.
478	What I just want you to see here, throughout the whole book, but also in this chapter, is that Rabbeinu Bachyei has something
479	precisely in the fact that he wrote these things a thousand years ago, that is so free of all the fakery
